content: The test image shows corn plants with lower leaves that are brown/dying while upper leaves remain green. I can see large areas of tan/brown leaf tissue - consistent with a foliar blight disease. Let me check the top candidate.

- Upper leaves remain green — disease progressing from bottom up

**Reference comparison (NCLB):**
- The reference shows characteristic cigar/canoe-shaped elongated tan to gray-brown lesions
- NCLB typically starts on lower leaves and progresses upward — matches the pattern in the test image
- When severe, NCLB destroys entire leaves causing the broad browning seen in the test image

The bottom-up progression and large tan/brown blighted lower leaves are classic for Northern corn leaf blight. The scale of browning suggests advanced/severe infection where multiple lesions have coalesced.
